INSTRUCTIONS

not have any unprinted or torn or missing pages or items, etc.  If so, get it replaced by a complete question
booklet of the same series.
2. Write and encode clearly the question booklet series A, B, C or D as the case may be in the appropriate
place in the OMR Answer Sheet.
3. Particulars/Details to be filled up in the OMR Answer Sheet should be filled up completely and
correctly, OMR Answer Sheet of candidates failing to do so will NOT be evaluated.
4. This Question Booklet contains  Section- ‘A’ & ‘B’. Section - ‘A’  should be answered only on the

5. After the examination has concluded, you should hand over the OMR and the Answer Sheet to the Invigilator

6. Separate sheets for rough work will be provided in the Examination Hall.

SECTION - A (Conventional Type) (40 Marks)
This Section should be answered only on the Answer Sheet provided.
Marks for each question is indicated against it. Attempt all questions.
1. Read the following passage carefully and write a precis in about one third of its length. Suggest a
suitable title.
(10)
In the modern world, money is often seen as the ultimate measure of success and security.
People devote their lives to earning more, believing that wealth guarantees happiness, comfort, and
respect. While money undoubtedly plays a crucial role in meeting basic needs and providing
opportunities, it is not the most important thing in life. Beyond a certain point, the pursuit of money
can lead to stress, unhealthy competition, and strained relationships.
True happiness and fulfillment often come from sources that money cannot buy—such as love,
health, peace of mind, and meaningful human connections. A wealthy person without friends or health
is not truly rich. Moreover, ethical values, compassion, and a sense of purpose add far more to a
person’s life than material possessions. The world has seen countless examples of individuals who,
despite limited means, lived content and impactful lives.
Money should be viewed as a tool, not a goal. It is meant to support life, not define it. A
balanced approach—where one earns enough for comfort but does not let money dictate all decisions—
is essential for a wholesome life. As societies evolve, there is a growing realization that quality of life
cannot be measured by income alone, but by the richness of experiences, relationships, and personal
growth.
2. Write a letter to the Engineer in Chief, Power and Electricity Department complaining about the
frequent breakdown of electricity in your locality. Sign yourself as Engliana.
(15)
3. Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows.
Exercise is essential for maintaining a healthy lifestyle. It helps improve cardiovascular health,
strengthens muscles, and boosts the immune system. Regular physical activity also reduces the risk of
chronic diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, and obesity. Additionally, exercise plays a crucial
role in mental well-being by reducing stress, anxiety, and depression.
There are different types of exercises, including aerobic exercises like running and swimming,
strength training like weightlifting, and flexibility exercises such as yoga and stretching. A combination
of these exercises ensures overall fitness and health. Experts recommend at least 30 minutes of
moderate exercise per day to maintain good health.
The lack of physical activity has become a major concern, especially with modern lifestyles that
involve sitting for long hours. Many people spend excessive time on screens, leading to a sedentary
lifestyle. This can result in weight gain, muscle weakness, and poor cardiovascular health. To stay
active, individuals can take small steps such as walking instead of driving, using stairs instead of
elevators, and participating in sports or outdoor activities.
Governments and health organizations promote exercise through awareness campaigns, fitness
programs, and policies that encourage active lifestyles. Schools also play a key role by including
physical education in their curriculum. Exercise is not just about fitness—it is a way to enhance the
quality of life and increase life expectancy.

(a) __________________ exercise includes activities like running and swimming
(1)
(b) A sedentary lifestyle can lead to __________________ gain
(1)

Direction (Question Nos 51 - 55) : Complete the sentence with the most suitable phrase :
51. No sooner had I reached the station ________
(a) when the train had already left
(b) than the train left
(c) then the train is leaving
(d) but the train is yet to leave
52. Had it not been for his timely intervention, ___________
(a) the situation would have worsened
(b) the situation is improving
(c) the problem was solved easily
(d) he will be appreciated

- 8 -
53. Not until the investigation was completed_____________
(a) the truth had already come out
(b) did the truth come to light
(c) the authorities knew the truth
(d) has the truth been revealed.
54. Only after years of training______________
(a) he can easily perform the task
(b) he is learning the technique
(c) was he able to master the skill
(d) he understands the importance of practice.
55. Little did they realize_________________
(a) and they had already anticipated the results.
(b) so they were prepared for the outcome
(c) that their decision would have long-term consequences
(d) since they understood the risk from the start.
Direction (Question Nos 56 - 60): Change the following into a conditional sentence.
56. She missed the bus because she left late.
(a) If she left on time, she would not miss the bus.
(b) If she had left on time, she would not have missed the bus.
(c) If she leaves on time, she will not miss the bus.
(d) If she had left on time, she will not miss the bus.
57. I don’t have enough money, so I can’t buy a car.
(a) If I had enough money, I would buy a car.
(b) If I have enough money I will buy a car.
(c) If I had had enough money, I would buy a car.
(d) If I had enough money, I will buy a car
58. You must study regularly to do well in exams.
(a) If you studied regularly, you will do well in exams.
(b) If you have studied regularly, you would have scored well.
(c) If you had studied regularly, you will score well.
(d) If you study regularly, you will score well in exams.
59. She is not careful, so she often makes mistakes.
(a) If she is careful, she will not make mistakes.
(b) If she was careful, she would not make mistakes.
(c) If she were careful, she would not make mistakes.
(d) If she had been careful, she would not make mistakes.
60. They speak too fast, so we cannot understand them.
(a) If they spoke slowly, we could understand them.
(b) If they speak slowly, we could understand them.
(c) If they had spoken slowly, we could understand them.
(d) If they would speak slowly, we could understand them.
